notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton.

John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt. That pair has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 87:24 together, about what it had with Marino (59%).

Nick Suzuki has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alex Newhook has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský. That line has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:23 together, down from 59% with Suzuki.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson. That pair has had 46% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 39:36 together, up from 41% with Matheson.
Nick Suzuki is expected back after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 20 points, the Canadiens tied for second in the Atlantic with 21 points.

MTL.head: The Canadiens face a real test
MTL.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Montréal has home-ice advantage and gets Suzuki back, and the Mammoth will be without Yamamoto. The Canadiens’ best way through is getting good looks.

story.head: Strength vs. Strength
paras: The Mammoth (10-6-0) beat Toronto 3-2 on Tuesday, while the Canadiens (9-3-3) lost 5-4 in overtime to Winnipeg the same night. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.625) says: their chances are worth about .747, and their goaltending has held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.700) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.558), largely because they’re 6-4 in one-goal games.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). As for the Canadiens, they get into more chippy games than anyone (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). Something has to give when the Canadiens’ shooting runs into the Mammoth’s defense, and the Mammoth’s power play (10th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (23rd).

Clayton Keller (4 G / 17 A / 21 P in 16 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Nick Schmaltz (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Cole Caufield (10 G / 4 A / 14 P in 15 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead. Lane Hutson (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 15 GP) shares it.
Sebastian Cossa (4-1-0 / .876 SV% in 5 GS) is expected to go for Utah. Jacob Fowler (7-1-1 / .925 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and is expected to start.
